- Elizabeth had been curt with him, and she told him it was due to personal stress, not anger at him.
- She accepted his coffee break offer and shared some details about her stress.
- He suggested professional help, and Elizabeth said she had thought about it but was hesitant.
- In scenario 4, he noticed she became slightly withdrawn after that suggestion. He believed his suggestion may have embarrassed her and felt regretful, so his intention was to apologize and reassure her of his good intentions.
- In scenario 5, Elizabeth responded appreciatively and seemed more open. Keith believes she values his support and feels more comfortable, so his intention becomes to maintain a supportive relationship and keep communication open.

Keith does not know:
- The full underlying facts of Elizabeth’s personal stress beyond what she chose to share.
- Whether she was actually embarrassed by his professional-help suggestion, only that he suspected it.
- Her private internal thoughts beyond her verbal responses and apparent openness.
- Whether she will actually seek professional help or how she truly feels deep down.

From Keith’s perspective, his intention does change from scenario 4 to scenario 5. In scenario 4, he wants to apologize and reassure Elizabeth that he meant well. In scenario 5, after her appreciative response, he wants to maintain a supportive relationship and keep communication open.
